title: Skewed link regression models for imbalanced binary response with applications to life insurance
authors_full: Shuang Yin; Dipak K. Dey; Emiliano A. Valdez; Guojun Gan; Jeyaraj Vadiveloo
summary: The paper explores skewed link regression models for imbalanced binary outcomes in life insurance mortality prediction, using Bayesian methods and real data to show improved performance over standard GLMs.
key_insight: Skewed link functions in Bayesian GLMs can better model rare mortality events in life insurance, but the focus on mortality rather than general insurance claims reserving limits its direct applicability to the working party's goals.

title: Automated Defect Identification and Categorization in NDE 4.0 with the Application of Artificial Intelligence
authors_full: Aditya Sharma
summary: This paper focuses on automated defect detection in industrial radiography using a modified U-Net model, with no connection to insurance claims reserving or actuarial practice.
key_insight: The research is entirely unrelated to claims reserving, loss modelling, or any actuarial application, making it of negligible relevance to the working party.

title: Aspect Classification for Legal Depositions
authors_full: Saurabh Chakravarty; Satvik Chekuri; Maanav Mehrotra; Edward A. Fox
summary: This paper develops a text classification system to identify semantic aspects in legal depositions, primarily for summarization and information retrieval in tort litigation contexts.
key_insight: While potentially useful for insurance claim agents reviewing deposition transcripts, the paper lacks direct application to claims reserving, reserve uncertainty, or predictive modeling of claim development.

title: DeepTriangle: A Deep Learning Approach to Loss Reserving
authors_full: Kevin Kuo
summary: DeepTriangle introduces a deep learning framework for loss reserving that jointly models paid losses and claims outstanding, requiring minimal feature engineering and outperforming traditional stochastic methods.
key_insight: The model's ability to automate forecasts and improve accuracy across lines of business makes it highly practical for actuarial reserving workflows.

title: Copula-based Modeling for IBNR Claim Loss Reserving
authors_full: Samira Zaroudi; Mohammad Reza Faridrohani; Mohammad Hassan Behzadi; Hadi Safari-Katesari
summary: This paper introduces a copula-based model to capture dependencies in IBNR claim timing and delay, validated via simulation and real auto insurer data, with comparison to the classical chain ladder method.
key_insight: Copula modeling of IBNR claim timing dependencies offers a practical, interpretable alternative to traditional methods with empirical validation against chain ladder.

title: Average-case Speedup for Product Formulas
authors_full: Chi-Fang; Chen; Fernando G. S. L. Brandão
summary: This paper explores theoretical improvements in quantum simulation using product formulas, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The paper demonstrates that product formulas for quantum simulation perform better on average-case inputs than worst-case bounds suggest, but this has no practical relevance to claims reserving.

title: Functional Analysis of Loss-development Patterns in P&C Insurance
authors_full: Arthur Charpentier; Qiheng Guo; Mike Ludkovski
summary: The paper applies functional data analysis to loss development triangles in workers' compensation, offering a probabilistic forecasting method with uncertainty quantification that outperforms Chain Ladder.
key_insight: Functional bootstrapping combined with PCA-based regression enables accurate joint uncertainty quantification for incomplete loss development curves, directly advancing practical reserving methodology.

title: Blockwise Missingness meets AI: A Tractable Solution for Semiparametric Inference
authors_full: Qi Xu; Lorenzo Testa; Jing Lei; Kathryn Roeder
summary: The paper introduces a semiparametric inference method for blockwise missing data using AI models, but it is not focused on claims reserving or insurance applications.
key_insight: The IBM(RAY) estimator improves efficiency over complete-case analysis for blockwise missing data, regardless of AI model accuracy, but lacks direct relevance to actuarial reserving contexts.

title: Dynamic and granular loss reserving with copulae
authors_full: Matúš Maciak; Ostap Okhrin; Michal Pešta
summary: This paper introduces a time-varying copula framework for granular, claim-level reserving to address limitations of aggregated triangle methods, with potential for improved reserve estimation across multiple lines of business.
key_insight: The proposed copula-based approach enables dynamic, micro-level reserving by modeling dependencies in individual claim development, offering a practical alternative to traditional aggregate methods.

title: Nonparametric modeling cash flows of insurance company
authors_full: Valery Baskakov; Nikolay Sheparnev; Evgeny Yanenko
summary: The paper introduces a nonparametric method for modeling insurance cash flows and estimating reserves including IBNR, validated against traditional actuarial methods using real Russian non-life data.
key_insight: The additive, claim-level estimation approach enables flexible reserve redistribution and financial reporting alignment while maintaining accuracy comparable to chain-ladder and Bornhuetter-Ferguson methods.

title: Mott transition and electronic excitation of the Gutzwiller wavefunction
authors_full: Masanori Kohno
summary: This paper explores the Mott transition in condensed matter physics using the Gutzwiller wavefunction and does not address claims reserving, actuarial science, or machine learning applications in insurance.
key_insight: The Mott transition is better understood as freezing of charge degrees of freedom while spin remains active, even under Fermi-liquid-like ground states.

title: Frequency-splitting estimators of single-propagator traces
authors_full: Leonardo Giusti; Tim Harris; Alessandro Nada; Stefan Schaefer
summary: This paper focuses on improving stochastic estimators for fermion traces in lattice QCD, with no connection to actuarial reserving, claims development, or insurance loss modeling.
key_insight: The proposed frequency-splitting estimators significantly reduce computational cost in quantum chromodynamics simulations but offer no practical value for general insurance reserving research.

title: Standard Errors for Calibrated Parameters
authors_full: Matthew D. Cocci; Mikkel Plagborg-Møller
summary: The paper develops conservative standard errors for calibrated structural models using only variances of empirical moments, with applications in macroeconomics, but does not address claims reserving or actuarial practice.
key_insight: Conservative standard errors can be derived without estimating moment correlations, offering robust inference under worst-case assumptions, though not tailored to reserving contexts.

title: Gradient Boosting for Spatial Panel Models with Random and Fixed Effects
authors_full: Michael Balzer; Adhen Benlahlou
summary: The paper introduces a gradient boosting framework for spatial panel models with fixed and random effects, applicable to non-life insurance data at a district level, though not focused on claims reserving or development triangles.
key_insight: Gradient boosting can handle high-dimensional spatial panel data with interpretable results and implicit regularization, offering potential for actuarial applications in geographically stratified loss modeling.

title: Modelling extreme claims via composite models and threshold selection methods
authors_full: Yinzhi Wang; Ingrid Hobæk Haff; Arne Huseby
summary: This paper explores composite models for extreme claims using threshold selection methods and evaluates their impact on reserve estimation, with a focus on bulk distribution choice and sample size effects.
key_insight: The square root rule performs best for reserve estimation with sufficient data, while simultaneous estimation excels in small samples, and bulk distribution choice significantly affects results—especially under heavy tails.

title: Distributionally Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Intelligent Traffic Control
authors_full: Shuwei Pei; Joran Borger; Arda Kosay; Muhammed O. Sayin; Saeed Ahmed
summary: This paper focuses on traffic signal control using multi-agent reinforcement learning and distributional robustness, with no connection to claims reserving, loss development, or actuarial modeling.
key_insight: The research advances robust traffic control under uncertain demand but offers no practical value or transferability to general insurance reserving.

title: Robust bootstrap procedures for the chain-ladder method
authors_full: Kris Peremans; Pieter Segaert; Stefan Van Aelst; Tim Verdonck
summary: This paper introduces robust bootstrap methods for the chain-ladder technique to improve reserve estimation under outlier contamination, with applications to one-year risk measures and validation on real and simulated data.
key_insight: Robust bootstrap procedures can meaningfully enhance the reliability of stochastic reserve estimates in the presence of outliers, offering practical value for actuarial reserving practice.

title: Quantitative measure for the spin-charge separation in two dimensional Hubbard model
authors_full: Amir Youssefi; M. Ansari-Fard; S. A. Jafari
summary: This paper introduces a quantitative measure for spin-charge separation in the 2D Hubbard model, focusing on condensed matter physics and non-equilibrium dynamics, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The paper's focus on quantum many-body systems and Mott insulators has no practical relevance to general insurance claims reserving or machine learning applications in actuarial science.

title: Long monotone trails in random edge-labelings of random graphs
authors_full: Omer Angel; Asaf Ferber; Benny Sudakov; Vincent Tassion
summary: This paper studies the asymptotic length of increasing trails and paths in randomly edge-labeled Erdős–Rényi graphs, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The paper provides theoretical results on random graph labelings and trail lengths, which are mathematically interesting but irrelevant to claims reserving or machine learning applications in actuarial science.

title: Building and Testing Yield Curve Generators for P&C Insurance
authors_full: Gary Venter; Kailan Shang
summary: The paper focuses on yield curve generators and interest rate risk for P&C insurers, with emphasis on bond valuation and capital impacts under GAAP, not claims reserving or loss development.
key_insight: This work addresses asset-side interest rate risk modeling for P&C insurers, which is tangential to the working party's focus on liability-side claims reserving and predictive modeling.

title: Adaptive Insurance Reserving with CVaR-Constrained Reinforcement Learning under Macroeconomic Regimes
authors_full: Stella C. Dong
summary: This paper frames reserving as a reinforcement learning problem under macroeconomic regimes, using CVaR-constrained PPO to optimize reserve adequacy and solvency while aligning with regulatory frameworks like Solvency II.
key_insight: Reinforcement learning with CVaR constraints can improve tail-risk control in reserving decisions under macroeconomic stress, offering a governance-aligned alternative to classical actuarial methods.

title: String tension and robustness of confinement properties of in the Schwinger-Thirring model
authors_full: Joao C. Pinto Barros; Marcello Dalmonte; Andrea Trombettoni
summary: This paper explores confinement properties in the Schwinger-Thirring model from a theoretical physics perspective, with no connection to actuarial science or claims reserving.
key_insight: The paper's findings on quantum field theory and string tension have no practical relevance to general insurance reserving or machine learning applications in actuarial practice.

title: "Worst-Case" Micro-Lensing in the Identification and Modeling of Lensed Quasars
authors_full: Luke Weisenbach; Paul Schechter; Sahil Pontula
summary: This paper addresses astrophysical micro-lensing effects in quasar observations and has no connection to actuarial claims reserving or insurance loss modelling.
key_insight: The paper quantifies worst-case micro-lensing uncertainties in astronomical imaging, which is entirely unrelated to general insurance reserving practice or methodology.

title: A non-convex regularization approach for stable estimation of loss development factors
authors_full: Himchan Jeong; Hyunwoong Chang; Emiliano A. Valdez
summary: The paper introduces a non-convex regularization method (LAAD penalty) to stabilize loss development factor estimation in claims reserving, demonstrating promising results on real P&C data with a provably convergent algorithm.
key_insight: LAAD-penalized regression improves stability and variable selection in estimating loss development factors, offering a practical, statistically grounded alternative to traditional methods for actuarial reserving.

title: ALTIS: Automated Loss Triage and Impact Scoring from Sentinel-1 SAR for Property-Level Flood Damage Assessment
authors_full: Amogh Vinaykumar; Prem Kamasani
summary: The paper introduces ALTIS, a satellite-based flood damage assessment system for property-level triage, aimed at reducing manual claims inspections but not directly addressing reserving or reserve estimation.
key_insight: ALTIS improves post-flood claims triage efficiency using SAR data but does not contribute to claims reserving, IBNR/RBNS estimation, or probabilistic reserve forecasting.

title: Mastering an Accurate and Generalizable Simulation-Based Method to Obtain Bias-corrected Point Estimates and Sampling Variance for Any Effect Sizes
author_surnames: Nakagawa; Mizuno; Williams; Ortega; Drobniak; Lagisz; Yang; Senior; Noble; Lundgren
authors_full: Shinichi Nakagawa; Ayumi Mizuno; Coralie Williams; Santiago Ortega; Szymon M. Drobniak; Malgorzata Lagisz; Yefeng Yang; Alistair M. Senior; Daniel W. A. Noble; Erick Lundgren
summary: The paper introduces a simulation-based bootstrap method (SAFE) for deriving bias-corrected effect size estimates and sampling variances in meta-analysis, primarily targeting statistical practitioners rather than actuarial reserving contexts.
key_insight: SAFE bootstrap simplifies variance estimation for arbitrary effect sizes via simulation, but lacks direct applicability to claims reserving, IBNR, or loss development modeling.

title: Connecting actuarial judgment to probabilistic learning techniques with graph theory
authors_full: Roland R. Ramsahai
summary: The paper explores using graphical models to represent actuarial judgment and probabilistic learning in non-life insurance claims, with potential for integrating telematics and dynamic data.
key_insight: Graphical models offer a structured, intuitive way to embed actuarial judgment into probabilistic reserving frameworks while enabling scalable inference on complex, interdependent claim variables.

title: Stochastic Claims Reserving Using State Space Modeling
authors_full: Rajesh Selukar
summary: This paper presents a statistically robust state space modeling framework for IBNR reserving, complete with Kalman filtering, smoothing, and simulation methods, demonstrated on real data with reproducible SAS code.
key_insight: State space models offer a transparent, probabilistic, and computationally tractable approach to claims reserving that integrates model fitting, diagnostics, and uncertainty quantification in a unified framework.

title: Shackling Uncertainty using Mixed Criticality in Monte-Carlo Tree Search
authors_full: Franco Cordeiro; Samuel Tardieu; Laurent Pautet
summary: The paper introduces a mixed criticality extension to Monte-Carlo Tree Search for embedded systems with uncertain resource costs, but it has no direct or transferable application to actuarial claims reserving.
key_insight: The method optimizes resource allocation under uncertainty in real-time systems, which is unrelated to insurance reserving problems.

title: A comparative analysis of several multivariate zero-inflated and zero-modified models with applications in insurance
authors_full: Pengcheng Zhang; David Pitt; Xueyuan Wu
summary: The paper explores multivariate zero-inflated and zero-modified models for modeling correlated claim frequencies across insurance lines, with empirical applications to automobile insurance data.
key_insight: Multivariate zero-modified models offer a flexible and robust approach to handling excess or deficient common zeros in correlated claim frequency data, which can improve reserving accuracy when modeling multiple lines of business.

title: Modeling frequency distribution above a priority in presence of IBNR
authors_full: Nicolas Baradel
summary: The paper addresses frequency modeling above a priority level in reinsurance, incorporating IBNR and using Schnieper's framework with Poisson and Negative Binomial distributions, plus bootstrap uncertainty quantification.
key_insight: Schnieper's model provides a consistent Poisson-based foundation for estimating claim frequencies above a priority, with bootstrap methods enhancing parameter uncertainty assessment in IBNR-inclusive settings.

title: A non-parametric estimator for Archimedean copulas under flexible censoring scenarios and an application to claims reserving
authors_full: Marie Michaelides; Hélène Cossette; Mathieu Pigeon
summary: The paper extends a non-parametric copula estimator to handle censored data and applies it to model dependence between correlated insurance coverages, with potential use in claims reserving workflows.
key_insight: Modeling dependence structures under flexible censoring using non-parametric copulas can enhance the realism of multilevel claims reserving models, especially when claim activation delays are correlated.

title: Fermi surface as a quantum critical manifold: gaplessness, order parameter, and scaling in d-dimensions
authors_full: Gennady Y. Chitov
summary: This paper explores quantum criticality and Fermi surfaces in fermionic systems, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The paper advances theoretical condensed matter physics by characterizing gapless phases via geometric order parameters and scaling laws near Lifshitz transitions, but offers no practical value for claims reserving.

title: Hamming and simplex codes for the sum-rank metric
authors_full: Umberto Martínez-Peñas
summary: This paper introduces sum-rank Hamming and simplex codes for error correction in multishot matrix-multiplicative channels, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The work is purely theoretical coding theory with no practical relevance to claims reserving, loss forecasting, or actuarial machine learning applications.

title: GraphCheck: Multipath Fact-Checking with Entity-Relationship Graphs
authors_full: Hyewon Jeon; Jay-Yoon Lee
summary: The paper introduces GraphCheck, a framework for multi-hop fact-checking using entity-relationship graphs, which is unrelated to claims reserving or actuarial modeling.
key_insight: This research focuses on automated textual fact-checking and offers no practical value or transferability to general insurance claims reserving.

title: Continuous chain-ladder with paid data
authors_full: Stephan M. Bischofberger; Munir Hiabu; Alex Isakson
summary: This paper reinterprets the chain-ladder method in continuous time using hazard functions and proposes kernel-smoothed alternatives, offering a theoretically grounded improvement with empirical validation on real data.
key_insight: Chain-ladder development factors can be viewed as histogram estimators of a cost-weighted hazard function, and replacing them with kernel smoothers improves consistency and predictive performance in reserving.

title: Minimax state estimates for abstract Neumann problems
authors_full: Alexander Nakonechnyi; Sergiy Zhuk
summary: The paper addresses minimax estimation for abstract Neumann problems in Hilbert spaces with uncertain inputs, which is mathematically rigorous but unrelated to actuarial reserving or insurance claim modeling.
key_insight: This theoretical work on partial differential equations and robust estimation has no practical application to claims reserving, IBNR, or machine learning in actuarial science.

title: On the impact of outliers in loss reserving
authors_full: Benjamin Avanzi; Mark Lavender; Greg Taylor; Bernard Wong
summary: This paper analyzes the sensitivity of loss reserving methods, particularly Mack's model and Bornhuetter-Ferguson, to outliers using impact functions, with empirical validation on real insurer data.
key_insight: Outliers disproportionately affect reserve estimates in Mack's model depending on their position in the triangle, highlighting the need for robustness checks in actuarial practice.

title: Parameter uncertainty and reserve risk under Solvency II
authors_full: Andreas Fröhlich; Annegret Weng
summary: The paper examines parameter uncertainty in reserve risk under Solvency II, critiquing bootstrapping and proposing an adapted method that better aligns with required confidence levels for solvency capital.
key_insight: Standard bootstrapping is inadequate for modeling parameter uncertainty under Solvency II, and a modified Froehlich-style approach better achieves the required confidence level for reserve risk capital.

title: A multistate approach to disability insurance reserving with information delays
authors_full: Oliver Lunding Sandqvist
summary: The paper introduces a multistate reserving model for disability insurance that accounts for real-time claim evolution and information delays, with parametric estimators and a real-data application.
key_insight: By decoupling available information from the underlying biometric process, the model enables more accurate individual-level reserving in disability insurance despite reporting and adjudication delays.

title: Predictive Claim Scores for Dynamic Multi-Product Risk Classification in Insurance
authors_full: Robert Matthijs Verschuren
summary: The paper extends Bonus-Malus models to incorporate multi-product claim scores for dynamic risk classification, focusing on pricing rather than reserving.
key_insight: Incorporating cross-product claim history improves risk classification for pricing but does not address claims reserving, IBNR, or reserve uncertainty.

title: Stochastic reserving with a stacked model based on a hybridized Artificial Neural Network
authors_full: Eduardo Ramos-Pérez; Pablo J. Alonso-González; José Javier Núñez-Velázquez
summary: This paper proposes a stacked machine learning model combining Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, and ANNs to improve runoff prediction in claims reserving, calibrated with a log-normal approach for uncertainty quantification.
key_insight: Stacking traditional actuarial models with ML algorithms can enhance reserve accuracy and risk assessment while maintaining interpretability through hybrid calibration.

title: Claim Reserving via Inverse Probability Weighting: A Micro-Level Chain-Ladder Method
authors_full: Sebastian Calcetero-Vanegas; Andrei L. Badescu; X. Sheldon Lin
summary: This paper bridges macro-level Chain-Ladder with micro-level data using inverse probability weighting, offering a statistically grounded extension that retains practicality for actuaries.
key_insight: The Chain-Ladder method is reinterpreted as a special case of an inverse probability weighted estimator, enabling incorporation of individual claim characteristics without sacrificing interpretability or statistical rigor.

title: A hierarchical reserving model for reported non-life insurance claims
authors_full: Jonas Crevecoeur; Jens Robben; Katrien Antonio
summary: This paper introduces a flexible hierarchical reserving model that integrates claim-specific covariates and development history, bridging aggregate and individual reserving approaches with practical validation on real and simulated data.
key_insight: The hierarchical framework enables data-driven selection between aggregate and individual reserving while incorporating machine learning methods to improve predictive accuracy and interpretability for non-life claims.

title: Existence of the first magic angle for the chiral model of bilayer graphene
authors_full: Alexander B. Watson; Mitchell Luskin
summary: This paper proves the existence of a flat band in the chiral model of twisted bilayer graphene at a specific twist angle, using mathematical analysis and computer-assisted proofs.
key_insight: The work confirms a theoretical prediction about electronic band structure in graphene physics, with no connection to actuarial reserving or machine learning applications in insurance.

title: Individual claims reserving using the Aalen-Johansen estimator
authors_full: Martin Bladt; Gabriele Pittarello
summary: The paper introduces a novel individual claims reserving method using the conditional Aalen-Johansen estimator, reinterpreting multi-state models to predict claim size development curves with validation on real and simulated data.
key_insight: By treating claim size as the state variable in a multi-state model, this approach enables probabilistic forecasting of individual claim development paths, offering strong transferability to micro-level reserving practice.

title: Modelling the term-structure of default risk under IFRS 9 within a multistate regression framework
authors_full: Arno Botha; Tanja Verster; Roland Breedt
summary: The paper models loan default risk over time using multistate regression techniques, with implications for IFRS 9 loss reserves in banking, but is not directly focused on general insurance claims reserving.
key_insight: While the multistate regression framework and diagnostics offer transferable methodological value, the focus on banking loan defaults under IFRS 9 limits its direct applicability to P&C claims reserving.

title: Synthetic Dataset Generation of Driver Telematics
authors_full: Banghee So; Jean-Philippe Boucher; Emiliano A. Valdez
summary: The paper generates a synthetic telematics dataset for usage-based insurance risk modeling, using neural networks and SMOTE to simulate claims counts and amounts, with validation against real data using GLMs.
key_insight: While the synthetic dataset could support reserving research if adapted, its primary focus on pricing/underwriting via telematics limits direct applicability to claims reserving without further methodological extension.

title: Mack's estimator motivated by large exposure asymptotics in a compound Poisson setting
authors_full: Nils Engler; Filip Lindskog
summary: This paper provides a theoretical justification for Mack's chain ladder estimator under compound Poisson models via large exposure asymptotics, strengthening its practical validity in reserving without requiring distribution-free assumptions.
key_insight: Mack's estimator can be rigorously derived and applied to compound Poisson loss models in the large exposure limit, offering a more defensible foundation for uncertainty quantification in traditional triangle-based reserving.

title: Statistical Learning of Trade Credit Insurance Network Data with Applications to Ratemaking and Reserving
authors_full: Woongchae Yoo; Spark C. Tseung; Tsz Chai Fung
summary: The paper develops a network-augmented GLMM for trade credit insurance data to jointly model claim probability and reporting delays, with applications to reserving and ratemaking.
key_insight: Incorporating network structure and random effects into a bivariate GLMM improves predictive accuracy for TCI reserving, offering a transferable framework for micro-level reserving in complex, relational insurance lines.

title: Non-parametric finite-sample credible intervals with one-dimensional priors: a middle ground between Bayesian and frequentist intervals
authors_full: Tim Ritmeester
summary: The paper introduces a new type of non-parametric credible interval that blends Bayesian and frequentist properties, using only one-dimensional priors for simplicity and practicality.
key_insight: This method offers a computationally simpler alternative to full Bayesian intervals while preserving interpretability and calibration, potentially useful for uncertainty quantification in reserving when high-dimensional priors are impractical.

title: A machine learning approach based on survival analysis for IBNR frequencies in non-life reserving
authors_full: Munir Hiabu; Emil Hofman; Gabriele Pittarello
summary: The paper introduces a survival analysis-based machine learning approach to forecast IBNR frequencies using individual claims data, with methods including Cox models, neural networks, and XGBoost, validated via simulation and real-world data.
key_insight: Modeling IBNR frequencies through hazard functions estimated via machine learning offers a flexible, granular, and coherent approach that improves upon traditional actuarial assumptions while maintaining practical interpretability.

title: Neural Methods for Multiple Systems Estimation Models
authors_full: Joseph Marsh; Nathan A. Judd; Lax Chan; Rowland G. Seymour
summary: The paper introduces neural Bayesian estimators for Multiple Systems Estimation to handle sparse, censored data in social science contexts like estimating hidden populations, but does not address claims reserving or insurance loss estimation.
key_insight: Neural Bayes and Posterior Estimators offer fast, robust inference for sparse administrative data in sociology, but lack direct applicability to actuarial reserving problems.

title: Towards Automatic Forecasting: Evaluation of Time-Series Forecasting Models for Chickenpox Cases Estimation in Hungary
authors_full: Wadie Skaf; Arzu Tosayeva; Dániel T. Várkonyi
summary: This paper evaluates time-series forecasting models, including LSTM and SARIMAX, for predicting chickenpox incidence in Hungary, with a focus on county- and national-level forecasts.
key_insight: While the paper demonstrates LSTM's superiority at county level and SARIMAX at national level, its health-domain application offers only weak transferability to actuarial claims reserving without adaptation.

title: Regret-Optimal Filtering for Prediction and Estimation
authors_full: Oron Sabag; Babak Hassibi
summary: The paper introduces regret-optimal filtering for signal estimation, positioning it between Kalman and H∞ filters, but does not connect to claims reserving, loss triangles, or actuarial forecasting.
key_insight: Regret-optimal filters offer a middle ground between average-case and worst-case performance but lack any application or transferability to actuarial reserving problems.

title: Parsimonious convolution quadrature
authors_full: Jens M. Melenk; Jörg Nick
summary: The paper introduces a computational method for accelerating convolution quadrature in Laplace-domain operator approximations, primarily targeting wave scattering problems in physics and engineering.
key_insight: This method reduces computational cost for time-domain simulations in physical systems but has no direct or transferable application to actuarial claims reserving or loss modelling.

title: Generalized Log-Normal Chain-Ladder
authors_full: D. Kuang; B. Nielsen
summary: This paper extends the log-normal chain-ladder model with asymptotic theory for distribution forecasting, offering improved uncertainty quantification and calibration compared to traditional methods like bootstrap or over-dispersed Poisson.
key_insight: The generalized log-normal chain-ladder model produces t-distributed forecast distributions under small σ asymptotics, providing a theoretically grounded alternative for reserve uncertainty estimation in aggregate triangle reserving.

title: Band Structures of Edge Magnetoplasmon Crystals
authors_full: Ken-ichi Sasaki
summary: This paper explores the band structures of edge magnetoplasmon crystals in condensed matter physics, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The research is entirely unrelated to claims reserving, machine learning applications in actuarial science, or any practical insurance context.

title: A Population Sampling Framework for Claim Reserving in General Insurance
authors_full: Sebastian Calcetero Vanegas; Andrei L. Badescu; X. Sheldon Lin
summary: This paper introduces a unified statistical framework for claim reserving based on population sampling theory, bridging macro- and micro-level approaches while addressing sampling bias in partially observed claims data.
key_insight: The paper's AIPW-based framework enables seamless integration of aggregate and individual claim models, offering actuaries more flexible, accurate, and statistically robust reserving tools.

title: A multivariate evolutionary generalised linear model framework with adaptive estimation for claims reserving
authors_full: Benjamin Avanzi; Gregory Clive Taylor; Phuong Anh Vu; Bernard Wong
summary: This paper extends GLMs for claims reserving by allowing dynamic, multi-dimensional factor evolution and cross-line dependence, using adaptive particle filtering for estimation, validated on real insurer data.
key_insight: The model's recursive, adaptive estimation of evolving factors across accident and calendar years improves reserve accuracy by capturing temporal dynamics and inter-line dependencies not addressed in traditional GLMs.

title: SPLICE: A Synthetic Paid Loss and Incurred Cost Experience Simulator
authors_full: Benjamin Avanzi; Gregory Clive Taylor; Melantha Wang
summary: SPLICE is a synthetic simulator for incurred loss estimates and claim revisions over time, designed to generate realistic individual-claim data for reserving research and model validation.
key_insight: SPLICE fills a critical gap by simulating case estimate dynamics and their dependencies on payments and ultimate claim size, enabling robust testing of micro-level reserving models.

title: Marked Cox Models for IBNR Claims Count: Continuous and Discretized Approaches with Dirichlet-Driven Reporting Delays
authors_full: Hassan Abdelrahman; Andrei Badescu; Radu Craiu; Sheldon Lin
summary: The paper introduces discrete-time Cox models with Dirichlet-driven reporting delays to improve IBNR claim count estimation, offering a flexible micro-level framework validated on auto-insurance data.
key_insight: Discrete-time Cox models incorporating Dirichlet-distributed reporting delays outperform continuous-time versions by jointly modeling delay and frequency, enhancing IBNR reserving accuracy.

title: Dynamic Financial Analysis (DFA) of General Insurers under Climate Change
authors_full: Benjamin Avanzi; Yanfeng Li; Greg Taylor; Bernard Wong
summary: The paper extends Dynamic Financial Analysis to incorporate climate change impacts on general insurers' assets and liabilities, using stochastic simulations and Australian data to benchmark against traditional DFA.
key_insight: Climate-dependent DFA reveals that physical and economic risk interactions significantly alter insurers' long-term risk-return profiles, but the framework is not directly applicable to claims reserving or loss development modeling.

title: Ground states of a nonlocal variational problem and Thomas-Fermi limit for the Choquard equation
authors_full: Damiano Greco; Yanghong Huang; Zeng Liu; Vitaly Moroz
summary: This paper studies nonlocal variational problems and ground states for the Choquard equation, with no connection to actuarial reserving, claims development, or insurance loss modeling.
key_insight: The work is purely mathematical and theoretical, focused on PDEs and functional inequalities, offering no practical value for claims reserving or actuarial machine learning applications.

title: Near-IR transmission spectrum of HAT-P-32 b using HST/WFC3
authors_full: M. Damiano; G. Morello; A. Tsiaras; T. Zingales; G. Tinetti
summary: This paper analyzes the near-infrared transit spectrum of exoplanet HAT-P-32b using Hubble Space Telescope data, focusing on atmospheric composition and retrieval methods.
key_insight: The study provides no relevance to actuarial claims reserving, as it is entirely focused on exoplanetary atmospheric science with no transferable methodology or application to insurance reserving.

title: Stochastic Loss Reserving: Dependence and Estimation
authors_full: Andrew Fleck; Edward Furman; Yang Shen
summary: The paper addresses dependence modeling in loss reserving using a modified continuous generalised method of moments to estimate parameters for complex distributions where MLE is impractical, with applications to stable and Tweedie-like models.
key_insight: CGMM provides a practical non-Bayesian estimation alternative for complex dependence structures in reserving when traditional likelihood-based methods fail.

title: A Unified Micro-Model for Loss Reserves, IBNR and Unearned Premium Risk with Dependence, Inflation, and Discounting
authors_full: Emmanuel Hamel; Anas Abdallah; Ghislain Léveillé
summary: This paper presents a unified micro-level stochastic framework for modeling loss reserves, IBNR, and unearned premium risk with dependence, inflation, and discounting, implemented via an Aggregate Trend Renewal Process and validated on medical malpractice data.
key_insight: The unified micro-model enables joint, forward-looking reserve and premium risk assessment under real-world dynamics like delay, inflation, and dependence—directly advancing practical reserving for long-tailed lines.

title: Replicating and extending chain-ladder via an age-period-cohort structure on the claim development in a run-off triangle
authors_full: Gabriele Pittarello; Munir Hiabu; Andrés M. Villegas
summary: The paper introduces a GLM-based model that replicates chain-ladder by modeling averaged hazard rates in reverse development time, reducing parameter complexity and enabling flexible extensions, with an accompanying R package for practical use on run-off triangles.
key_insight: Modeling claim development via reversed-time hazard rates in a GLM framework offers a simpler, more interpretable alternative to traditional claim-amount modeling while preserving chain-ladder logic and enabling richer extensions.

title: Endpoint estimates for maximal operators associated to the wave equation
authors_full: Chu-Hee Cho; Sanghyuk Lee; Wenjuan Li
summary: This paper addresses endpoint estimates for maximal operators in the context of the wave equation, a topic in harmonic analysis with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The paper resolves open endpoint bounds for maximal operators associated with the wave equation, but offers no practical relevance to claims reserving or machine learning applications in actuarial science.

title: On the evolution of data breach reporting patterns and frequency in the United States: a cross-state analysis
authors_full: Benjamin Avanzi; Xingyun Tan; Greg Taylor; Bernard Wong
summary: The paper models data breach frequency and IBNR estimation across U.S. states using notification laws, offering transferable methods for actuarial reserving in cyber insurance.
key_insight: By controlling for reporting patterns and state-specific notification laws, the paper provides a reliable method to estimate IBNR and trend shifts in cyber risk, which is directly applicable to reserving in cyber insurance.

title: Explainable Boosting Machine for Predicting Claim Severity and Frequency in Car Insurance
authors_full: Markéta Krùpovà; Nabil Rachdi; Quentin Guibert
summary: The paper applies the Explainable Boosting Machine (EBM) to car insurance claim frequency and severity, offering strong interpretability and performance compared to GLMs and XGBoost, with potential transferability to reserving contexts.
key_insight: EBM provides a high-performing, intrinsically interpretable alternative to traditional actuarial models, making it a practical candidate for enhancing transparency in claim prediction tasks relevant to reserving.

title: A new perspective from a Dirichlet model for forecasting outstanding liabilities of nonlife insurers
authors_full: Karthik Sriram; Peng Shi
summary: The paper introduces a Dirichlet model that unifies Chain-Ladder and Bornhuetter-Ferguson methods under a single statistical framework, offering flexible inference based on available data and validated on real workers' compensation claims.
key_insight: The Dirichlet model provides a statistically principled bridge between two classic reserving methods, enabling data-driven selection and improving interpretability and consistency in reserve forecasting.

title: κ-Explorer: A Unified Framework for Active Model Estimation in MDPs
authors_full: Xihe Gu; Urbashi Mitra; Tara Javidi
summary: The paper introduces κ-Explorer, an active exploration algorithm for Markov decision processes that optimizes state-action visitation based on estimation complexity, with applications in reinforcement learning but no direct link to claims reserving.
key_insight: κ-Explorer improves model estimation in MDPs by prioritizing high-variance, underexplored transitions, but offers no practical value or transferability to actuarial reserving problems.

title: Enhanced Gradient Boosting for Zero-Inflated Insurance Claims and Comparative Analysis of CatBoost, XGBoost, and LightGBM
authors_full: Banghee So
summary: The paper evaluates gradient boosting methods for zero-inflated claim frequency modeling, proposing a new zero-inflated Poisson boosted tree model and finding CatBoost performs best on telematics data.
key_insight: CatBoost-based zero-inflated Poisson models offer improved predictive performance for auto claim frequency, particularly with telematics data, though the focus is on frequency rather than reserving or severity.

title: Efficient estimation of parameters in marginals in semiparametric multivariate models
authors_full: Ivan Medovikov; Valentyn Panchenko; Artem Prokhorov
summary: The paper introduces a sieve MLE estimator for semiparametric multivariate models with known marginals, showing improved efficiency and robustness over QMLE and misspecified full MLE, with an insurance application involving censored claim loss data.
key_insight: The sieve MLE estimator offers a practical, robust alternative for parameter estimation in multivariate insurance models with censored variables, improving precision without requiring full copula specification.

title: Sparse Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SSUR) Copula Mixed Models for Multivariate Loss Reserving
authors_full: Pengfei Cai; Anas Abdallah; Pratheepa Jeganathan
summary: This paper introduces a sparse SUR copula mixed model for multivariate loss reserving that improves reserve accuracy and risk diversification while preserving interpretability of dependencies across lines of business and companies.
key_insight: The model combines random effects, LASSO shrinkage, and copula-based dependence to deliver interpretable, robust, and accurate multivariate reserve estimates with quantified risk capital benefits.

title: Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Loss Reserving and Risk Capital Analysis
authors_full: Pengfei Cai; Anas Abdallah; Pratheepa Jeganathan
summary: This paper introduces a recurrent neural network (Deep Triangle) and GAN-based extension for multivariate loss reserving, capturing dependencies across lines of business and generating predictive reserve distributions with improved performance over copula models.
key_insight: The extended Deep Triangle framework outperforms traditional copula regression in predicting total loss reserves and reveals greater diversification benefits through more accurate risk capital estimates.

title: The hierarchical generalized linear model and the bootstrap estimator of the error of prediction of loss reserves in a non-life insurance company
authors_full: Alicja Wolny-Dominiak
summary: This paper applies hierarchical generalized linear models to loss reserving and introduces a bootstrap estimator for prediction error, with full R code provided for reproducibility.
key_insight: The bootstrap-based error estimation offers a practical, interpretable way to quantify reserve uncertainty in HGLMs, directly addressing actuarial needs for robust prediction intervals.

title: Micro-level Reserving for General Insurance Claims using a Long Short-Term Memory Network
authors_full: Ihsan Chaoubi; Camille Besse; Hélène Cossette; Marie-Pier Côté
summary: This paper applies LSTM networks to micro-level reserving by modeling individual claim payments and recoveries over time, with adjustments for extreme values, and benchmarks against chain-ladder on real and simulated data.
key_insight: LSTM networks can effectively model granular claim dynamics at the individual level, offering a practical, data-driven alternative to aggregate triangle methods while explicitly handling tail risk.

title: The value of partial information
authors_full: Philip A. Ernst; Oleksii Mostovyi
summary: The paper explores pricing rules under partial information in jump-diffusion models, focusing on contingent claims and labor income streams, with no direct application to actuarial reserving or claim development.
key_insight: Partial information about jumps alters pricing for contingent liabilities, but the framework lacks connection to claims reserving, IBNR/RBNS estimation, or practical actuarial modeling.

title: Generalized XGBoost Method
authors_full: Yang Guang
summary: The paper extends XGBoost to support non-convex and multivariate loss functions, with examples in non-life insurance pricing, offering potential transferability to reserving if adapted to claim development or uncertainty modeling.
key_insight: Generalized XGBoost enables flexible, multi-parameter modeling of probability distributions using tree boosting, which could be repurposed for actuarial reserving tasks like IBNR estimation or probabilistic forecasting.

title: On the use of case estimate and transactional payment data in neural networks for individual loss reserving
authors_full: Benjamin Avanzi; Matthew Lambrianidis; Greg Taylor; Bernard Wong
summary: This paper evaluates neural network architectures for individual loss reserving using payment and case estimate data, finding that case estimates significantly improve predictions while recurrent structures offer only marginal gains.
key_insight: Case estimates provide substantial predictive value in individual reserving models, whereas adding memory via RNNs yields minimal improvement over feed-forward networks.

title: On the Sins of Image Synthesis Loss for Self-supervised Depth Estimation
author_surnames: Li; Drenkow; Ding; Ding; Lu; Creighton; Taylor; Unberath
authors_full: Zhaoshuo Li; Nathan Drenkow; Hao Ding; Andy S. Ding; Alexander Lu; Francis X. Creighton; Russell H. Taylor; Mathias Unberath
summary: This paper investigates the disconnect between image synthesis quality and depth estimation accuracy in self-supervised learning, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: Optimizing for image synthesis does not improve depth estimation and may even degrade it due to aleatoric uncertainty, a finding irrelevant to claims reserving.

title: User-click Modelling for Predicting Purchase Intent
authors_full: Simone Borg Bruun
summary: This paper models user-click behavior to predict insurance purchase intent using neural networks, but it focuses on marketing and underwriting rather than claims reserving or loss development.
key_insight: User-click patterns can predict purchase intent better than demographic data, but this has minimal direct relevance to actuarial reserving practice.

title: A Feasibility-Enhanced Control Barrier Function Method for Multi-UAV Collision Avoidance
author_surnames: Zhong; Wu; Yang; Xiao; Wu; Jiang; Fang
authors_full: Qishen Zhong; Junlong Wu; Jian Yang; Guanwei Xiao; Junqi Wu; Zimeng Jiang; Pingan Fang
summary: This paper focuses on multi-UAV collision avoidance using control barrier functions and has no connection to actuarial claims reserving or loss modelling.
key_insight: The research addresses technical feasibility in UAV control systems and offers no practical value for general insurance reserving or actuarial machine learning applications.

title: Exploration and Incentivizing Participation in Randomized Trials
authors_full: Yingkai Li; Aleksandrs Slivkins
summary: The paper addresses incentive design in randomized controlled trials, focusing on balancing exploration and exploitation for participant engagement, with no connection to claims reserving or actuarial practice.
key_insight: The paper proposes an incentive-compatible mechanism for RCTs that minimizes worst-case estimation error under adversarial outcomes, but offers no relevance to insurance reserving or actuarial modeling.

title: Dynamic online prediction model and its application to automobile claim frequency data
authors_full: Jiakun Jiang; Zhengxiao Li; Liang Yang
summary: The paper introduces a Dynamic Poisson State Space model for updating claim frequency predictions over time using smoothing splines, applied to Chinese auto insurance data with improved accuracy over existing methods.
key_insight: While the model offers dynamic updating and improved prediction for claim frequency, its focus on pricing-related frequency modeling rather than reserving or loss development limits its direct practical value to the IFoA reserving working party.

title: Model error and its estimation, with particular application to loss reserving
authors_full: G Taylor; G McGuire
summary: The paper addresses model error in loss reserving using Bayesian model averaging and LASSO-based methods, offering a practical framework to quantify uncertainty beyond traditional parameter and process errors.
key_insight: Internal model error can be estimated via Bayesian model averaging with bootstrapped LASSO, providing a more complete picture of reserve uncertainty that is directly applicable to actuarial practice.

title: Stochastic loss reserving with mixture density neural networks
authors_full: Muhammed Taher Al-Mudafer; Benjamin Avanzi; Greg Taylor; Bernard Wong
summary: This paper applies Mixture Density Networks to loss reserving, delivering both accurate central estimates and flexible quantile forecasts, with extensions for hybrid GLM integration and actuarial judgment constraints.
key_insight: MDNs provide a practical, distributionally rich framework for aggregate triangle reserving that outperforms classical models while allowing for actuarial input and interpretability.

title: JADE: Expert-Grounded Dynamic Evaluation for Open-Ended Professional Tasks
author_surnames: Lin; Liu; Yang; Cai; Xu; Wei; Xie; Zhang
authors_full: Lanbo Lin; Jiayao Liu; Tianyuan Yang; Li Cai; Yuanwu Xu; Lei Wei; Sicong Xie; Guannan Zhang
summary: The paper introduces JADE, a dynamic evaluation framework for agentic AI in professional tasks, using expert-grounded criteria and claim-level assessment, but it is not focused on claims reserving or actuarial applications.
key_insight: JADE improves evaluation stability for open-ended professional tasks by combining predefined expert skills with flexible, evidence-gated claim-level analysis, though it lacks direct relevance to actuarial reserving.

title: Bayesian Non-Negative Matrix Factorization with Correlated Mutation Type Probabilities for Mutational Signatures
authors_full: Iris Lang; Jenna Landy; Giovanni Parmigiani
summary: This paper introduces Bayesian NMF methods with correlated mutation type probabilities for cancer mutational signature analysis, which is unrelated to actuarial claims reserving.
key_insight: The paper advances cancer genomics by modeling dependencies in mutation signatures but offers no practical value or transferability to general insurance reserving.

title: Privacy-Enhancing Collaborative Information Sharing through Federated Learning - A Case of the Insurance Industry
author_surnames: Dong; Quan; Edwards; Wang; Feng; Wang; Foley; Shah
authors_full: Panyi Dong; Zhiyu Quan; Brandon Edwards; Shih-han Wang; Runhuan Feng; Tianyang Wang; Patrick Foley; Prashant Shah
summary: The paper explores federated learning for collaborative claims loss modeling across insurers without sharing raw data, addressing data scarcity and privacy concerns.
key_insight: Federated learning enables improved claims loss forecasting by aggregating insights from multiple insurers' private datasets while preserving data privacy.

title: Frequency-Severity Experience Rating based on Latent Markovian Risk Profiles
authors_full: Robert Matthijs Verschuren
summary: The paper introduces a latent Markovian model for joint frequency-severity experience rating in auto insurance, focusing on dynamic risk profiling rather than reserving.
key_insight: While innovative for pricing and segmentation, the paper's focus on premium calculation via latent risk profiles offers limited direct value to claims reserving or reserve uncertainty quantification.

title: Optimal relativities in a modified Bonus-Malus system with long memory transition rules and frequency-severity dependence
authors_full: Jae Youn Ahn; Eric C. K. Cheung; Rosy Oh; Jae-Kyung Woo
summary: The paper explores a modified Bonus-Malus System that incorporates multi-year claim history and frequency-severity dependence, primarily for premium rating rather than claims reserving.
key_insight: While methodologically interesting, the paper focuses on pricing and risk classification, not on estimating future claims reserves or modelling claim development patterns relevant to actuarial reserving.

title: Error analysis for 2D stochastic Navier-Stokes equations in bounded domains with Dirichlet data
authors_full: Dominic Breit; Andreas Prohl
summary: This paper focuses on numerical analysis of stochastic Navier-Stokes equations in fluid dynamics, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The work advances finite-element discretisation for stochastic PDEs in bounded domains but offers no practical relevance to claims reserving or general insurance actuarial practice.

title: A nested divide-and-conquer method for tensor Sylvester equations with positive definite hierarchically semiseparable coefficients
authors_full: Stefano Massei; Leonardo Robol
summary: This paper presents a numerical method for solving tensor Sylvester equations with specific matrix structures, focusing on computational efficiency and theoretical error bounds.
key_insight: The proposed nested divide-and-conquer algorithm achieves quasi-optimal complexity for solving structured tensor linear systems but has no direct or transferable application to actuarial claims reserving.

title: Ruin probability for renewal risk models with neutral net profit condition
authors_full: Andrius Grigutis; Arvydas Karbonskis; Jonas Šiaulys
summary: This paper explores ruin probability under neutral net profit conditions in classical and generalized renewal risk models, focusing on theoretical guarantees of ruin rather than claims reserving or loss forecasting.
key_insight: The paper proves that ruin is inevitable under a neutral net profit condition in certain renewal risk models, but offers no practical tools or insights for actuarial reserving or probabilistic reserve estimation.

title: Negative binomial models for development triangles of counts
authors_full: Luis E. Nieto-Barajas; Rodrigo S. Targino
summary: This paper introduces negative binomial models for predicting outstanding claim counts in development triangles, explicitly addressing overdispersion and dependence across development years with Bayesian inference.
key_insight: Negative binomial models offer a flexible, parametric alternative to chain ladder and overdispersed Poisson for modeling claim counts in triangles, with explicit handling of overdispersion and temporal dependence.

title: Continuous-time modeling and bootstrap for Schnieper's reserving
authors_full: Nicolas Baradel
summary: The paper extends Schnieper's IBNR/IBNER decomposition with a continuous-time stochastic model and bootstrap method for reserve uncertainty, offering a practical, distributional approach aligned with actuarial reserving principles.
key_insight: A continuous-time framework with Poisson and Brownian drivers enables realistic, non-negative, asymmetric reserve distributions without ad hoc assumptions, directly enhancing Schnieper-based reserving practice.

title: Asymptotically Optimal Locally Private Heavy Hitters via Parameterized Sketches
authors_full: Hao Wu; Anthony Wirth
summary: This paper focuses on locally private algorithms for frequency estimation and heavy hitters identification, with no connection to claims reserving, loss development, or actuarial modeling.
key_insight: The paper advances differential privacy techniques for frequency estimation but offers no practical value or transferability to actuarial reserving research or practice.

authors_full: Samuel M. Greene; Robert J. Webber; James E. T. Smith; Jonathan Weare; Timothy C. Berkelbach
summary: This paper presents a quantum Monte Carlo method for calculating excited-state energies in molecular systems, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The method improves accuracy in quantum chemistry simulations but offers no practical value for claims reserving or general insurance actuarial research.

title: From Chain-Ladder to Individual Claims Reserving
authors_full: Ronald Richman; Mario V. Wüthrich
summary: This paper reinterprets the chain-ladder method to enable direct projection of latest claims to ultimate, creating a bridge to individual-claim reserving with neural networks.
key_insight: Reframing chain-ladder as multi-period direct projection unlocks practical machine learning applications for individual claim reserving while preserving actuarial interpretability.

title: Check-COVID: Fact-Checking COVID-19 News Claims with Scientific Evidence
author_surnames: Wang; Harwood; Chillrud; Ananthram; Subbiah; McKeown
authors_full: Gengyu Wang; Kate Harwood; Lawrence Chillrud; Amith Ananthram; Melanie Subbiah; Kathleen McKeown
summary: This paper introduces a fact-checking benchmark for COVID-19 news claims using scientific evidence, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claim development.
key_insight: The research focuses on natural language processing for fact-checking in public health and has no practical relevance to claims reserving or general insurance actuarial practice.

title: Bounded Coupled AI Learning Dynamics in Tri-Hierarchical Drone Swarms
authors_full: Oleksii Bychkov
summary: This paper studies theoretical convergence and boundedness properties of multi-agent learning dynamics in drone swarms, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The paper provides formal guarantees for stability in tri-hierarchical AI learning systems but offers no practical relevance to claims reserving, loss modeling, or actuarial applications.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Micro-Level Claims Reserving
authors_full: Benjamin Avanzi; Ronald Richman; Bernard Wong; Mario Wüthrich; Yagebu Xie
summary: This paper frames individual claims reserving as a reinforcement learning problem, enabling sequential updates to reserve estimates using all claim trajectories—including open claims—and introduces actuarial-friendly components like rolling-settlement tuning and importance weighting for large claims.
key_insight: Reinforcement learning can improve micro-level reserving by learning from incomplete claim histories and producing stable, accurate reserve revisions over time, especially for immature claims.

title: Expected Complexity of Persistence Barcode Computation via Matrix Reduction
authors_full: Barbara Giunti; Guillaume Houry; Michael Kerber; Matthias Söls
summary: This paper focuses on the computational complexity of persistence barcodes in topological data analysis, with no connection to claims reserving, actuarial science, or insurance loss modeling.
key_insight: The paper provides theoretical bounds on matrix reduction complexity for random filtrations in topological data analysis, which has no practical relevance to actuarial reserving.

title: Modeling premiums of non-life insurance companies in India
authors_full: Kartik Sethi; Siddhartha P. Chakrabarty
summary: The paper fits extreme value distributions to non-life insurance premium data in India, with no focus on claims reserving, development triangles, or reserve uncertainty.
key_insight: Generalized Extreme Value distribution best fits Indian non-life premium data, but the analysis lacks relevance to actuarial reserving practice.

title: Six loop critical exponent analysis for Lee-Yang and percolation theory
authors_full: J. A. Gracey
summary: This paper focuses on theoretical physics, specifically critical exponent analysis in Lee-Yang and percolation theory using renormalization group methods, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The paper advances theoretical physics through six-loop renormalization analysis but offers no practical relevance to claims reserving, loss modeling, or actuarial machine learning.

title: Existence of a classical solution to the integro-differential equation arising in the Cramér-Lundberg non-life insurance model with proportional investment
authors_full: Platon Promyslov
summary: The paper proves the existence of a classical solution to an integro-differential equation in a Cramér–Lundberg model with proportional investment, focusing on survival probability under minimal moment conditions.
key_insight: While mathematically rigorous, the paper addresses ruin theory and investment dynamics rather than claims reserving, making it of limited practical relevance to the IFoA working party's focus.

title: Extremum Seeking Control with an Adaptive Gain Based On Gradient Estimation Error
authors_full: Claus Danielson; Scott A. Bortoff; Ankush Chakrabarty
summary: This paper focuses on extremum seeking control with adaptive gain for dynamic systems, unrelated to claims reserving or actuarial modeling.
key_insight: The method improves controller stability using gradient estimation error but has no practical application to insurance reserving or loss prediction.

title: Measuring and Mitigating Biases in Motor Insurance Pricing
authors_full: Mulah Moriah; Franck Vermet; Arthur Charpentier
summary: This paper focuses on fairness and bias mitigation in motor insurance pricing, not claims reserving or loss estimation.
key_insight: The study provides tools to measure and mitigate ethical biases in pricing but offers no practical value for actuarial reserving research or practice.

title: Towards Resilient Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles: A Distributionally Robust Input and State Estimation Approach
authors_full: Kasra Azizi; Kumar Anurag; Wenbin Wan
summary: This paper focuses on robust state estimation for autonomous vehicles under uncertainty, with no direct application to actuarial claims reserving or loss development modeling.
key_insight: The method improves resilience in dynamic systems but lacks transferability to insurance reserving contexts.

title: Ruin probabilities with investments: smoothness, IDE and ODE, asymptotic behavior
authors_full: Yuri Kabanov; Nikita Pukhlyakov
summary: This paper studies ruin probabilities for an insurer with life and non-life branches investing in risky assets, deriving smoothness properties and differential equations for ruin probability under exponential jumps.
key_insight: The paper provides theoretical results on ruin probability decay under investment risk but does not address claims reserving, IBNR/RBNS, or practical actuarial forecasting methods.

title: Asymmetric fitting function for condensed-phase Raman spectroscopy
authors_full: Vitaly I. Korepanov; Darya M. Sedlovets
summary: This paper introduces an asymmetric fitting function for Raman spectroscopy in condensed matter physics, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.
key_insight: The proposed asymmetric pseudo-Voigt function improves spectral peak fitting in materials science but offers no practical value for claims reserving or actuarial machine learning.

title: Bonus-malus Systems vs Delays in Claims Reporting and Settlement: Analysis of Ruin Probabilities
authors_full: Dhiti Osatakul; Shuanming Li; Xueyuan Wu
summary: The paper models ruin probabilities under bonus-malus systems with delayed by-claims, focusing on premium adjustments and correlation effects rather than reserving methodology or claim development.
key_insight: Delayed settlement of by-claims can paradoxically reduce ruin probabilities, but the paper's focus on pricing and risk models limits its direct applicability to claims reserving practice.

title: Estimation of the detected background by the future gamma-ray transient mission CAMELOT
author_surnames: Ripa; Galgóczi; Werner; Pál; Ohno; Mészáros; Mizuno; Tarcai; Torigoe; Uchida; Fukazawa; Takahashi; Nakazawa; Hirade; Hirose; Hisadomi; Enoto; Odaka; Ichinohe; Frei; Kiss

title: Model Monitoring: A General Framework with an Application to Non-life Insurance Pricing

summary: The paper presents a model monitoring framework for non-life insurance pricing, focusing on concept drift detection using Gini scores and calibration tests, with limited direct application to claims reserving.
key_insight: While methodologically rigorous, the paper's focus on pricing model monitoring offers only indirect relevance to reserving, as it does not address claim development, IBNR/RBNS, or reserve uncertainty quantification.

authors_full: Rares-Darius Buhai; Jun-Ting Hsieh; Aayush Jain; Pravesh K. Kothari
summary: This paper disproves a theoretical conjecture in average-case complexity related to low-degree moments and distinguishing algorithms, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.

title: Parametric estimation of conditional Archimedean copula generators for censored data
authors_full: Marie Michaelides; Hélène Cossette; Mathieu Pigeon
summary: The paper introduces a conditional Archimedean copula generator estimation method for censored data, applied to claims reserving to better capture dependence structures influenced by covariates.

title: SimLBR: Learning to Detect Fake Images by Learning to Detect Real Images

summary: This paper focuses on detecting AI-generated fake images using a novel regularization technique, with no connection to claims reserving, loss modelling, or actuarial applications.

title: From academic to media capital: To what extent does the scientific reputation of universities translate into Wikipedia attention?

summary: This paper examines how scientific reputation of universities correlates with Wikipedia attention, using Leiden Ranking indicators and analyzing regional and linguistic variations.

title: Using AoI Forecasts in Communicating and Robust Distributed Model-Predictive Control
authors_full: Jannik Hahn; Richard Schoeffauer; Gerhard Wunder; Olaf Stursberg
summary: This paper focuses on distributed control systems and communication scheduling in cyber-physical systems, with no connection to actuarial reserving or insurance claims modeling.

title: A Laplace transform-based test for the equality of positive semidefinite matrix distributions
authors_full: Žikica Lukić
summary: The paper introduces a statistical test for comparing matrix distributions using Laplace transforms, with applications demonstrated on insurance data, but does not focus on claims reserving or reserve estimation.
key_insight: While applicable to insurance data, the method lacks direct relevance to actuarial reserving tasks such as IBNR estimation, claim development modeling, or probabilistic forecasting.

title: A Subsampling Line-Search Method with Second-Order Results
authors_full: El-houcine Bergou; Youssef Diouane; Vladimir Kunc; Vyacheslav Kungurtsev; Clément W. Royer
summary: This paper presents a stochastic optimization method using subsampling and line-search for nonconvex problems, with theoretical guarantees and empirical results on general machine learning tasks.
key_insight: The method enables efficient escape from saddle points in nonconvex optimization using subsampled gradients and Newton-type directions, but offers no direct application or validation in claims reserving contexts.

title: Skewness-Robust Causal Discovery in Location-Scale Noise Models
authors_full: Daniel Klippert; Alexander Marx
summary: The paper introduces SkewD, a causal discovery method for location-scale noise models that handles skewed noise distributions, improving reliability over normal-distribution-based approaches in bivariate settings.

authors_full: Seung Min Baik; Eunshin Byon; Young Myoung Ko

title: Generative Synthesis of Insurance Datasets
authors_full: Kevin Kuo
summary: The paper introduces a CTGAN-based workflow to generate synthetic insurance datasets, evaluated for ML efficacy and statistical fidelity, with an R interface to encourage adoption by actuaries.
key_insight: Synthetic insurance datasets generated via CTGAN can support actuarial research and model development when real data is unavailable, provided they preserve key statistical properties and model stability.

title: Regular variation of a random length sequence of random variables and application to risk assessment
authors_full: Charles Tillier; Olivier Wintenberger
summary: The paper develops a theoretical framework for regular variation of random-length sequences and applies it to risk measures, including a brief mention of non-life insurance applications.

title: Measurements of the Safety Function Response Time on a Private 5G and IO-Link Wireless Testbed
authors_full: Henry Beuster; Kevin Tebbe; Thomas Doebbert; Gerd Scholl
summary: This paper focuses on safety function response times in industrial automation using private 5G and IO-Link Wireless, with no connection to actuarial claims reserving or loss modelling.

title: Zero-shot Fact Verification by Claim Generation
authors_full: Liangming Pan; Wenhu Chen; Wenhan Xiong; Min-Yen Kan; William Yang Wang
summary: This paper introduces a method for generating synthetic claims to train fact verification models, reducing reliance on manually annotated data, but it is unrelated to insurance claims reserving or actuarial practice.
